body.p: The present application has been reviewed in light of the Office Action dated March 28,
2024. Claims 50-68 are pending and rejected. Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the amendments and remarks made herein.
At the outset, Applicant thanks Examiner Woldemaryam for extending the courtesy of a

telephone interview with Applicant's undersigned representative on September 18, 2024. During the interview, agreement was reached that the drawings show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Further, agreement was reached that the claimed subject matter is described sufficiently in the specification so as to meet the written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). The discussion held during the interview is expanded on in the remarks below. The remarks below include particular citations to exemplary evidence supporting the sufficiency of the drawings and the sufficiency of the description with regards to the written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a), as requested by the Examiner.
Objections to the Drawings

The drawings are objected to under 37 C.F.R. 1.83(a) for allegedly failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims, in particular the recitation in claim 50, "...wherein the at least one cargo support segment comprises a fixed central region and opposing lateral end segments moveably coupled to the fixed region and moveable between a first position and a second position, the first position defining a first width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the constricted width and the second position defining a second width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the nominal width and greater than the constricted width..." and similar recitations in claim 60. The drawings support such recitations.
As agreed upon with the Examiner during the interview, at least one exemplary

embodiment of these claim recitations is shown in FIGS. 9A and 9B. Specifically, FIGS. 9A and 9B illustrate an exemplary embodiment of a cargo support segment that includes a fixed central region and opposing lateral end segments that are movable between positions defining various widths. The
illustrations of these figures are expanded on in the as-filed specification, which states, for example, at paragraph [0108] of the U.S. publication:

In FIGS. 9A and 9B, a cargo bay floor segment 502' includes a stationary region 505 that is coupled with the rails 174 and a moveable lateral end 503 that is rotatable about a hinge connection 504 with the stationary region. In this manner, and as shown, the moveable lateral end 503 can be rotated to move out of the way of the wheel well 579 and enable the cargo bay floor segment 502' to advance into the aft region of the cargo

bay 170. FIGS. 9 SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.2772.867 502' can include
sides, enabling the cargo bay floor segment 502' to move past the opposing wheel wells 579, thereby reduce a minimum lateral clearance of the cargo floor segment 502. Similarly, as the cargo bay 170 may taper, especially in the aft region 170 a, the cargo bay floor segment 502 can have different shapes that enable each cargo bay floor segment 502 to fit into a

p.u: different position along the cargo bay 170.

body.p: In other words, the movable lateral ends 503 can be rotated about the hinge connection 504 to change the overall shape and width of the cargo bay floor segment 502, thus allowing the cargo bay floor segment 502 to fit within the cargo bay 170 at different positions along the cargo bay 170 (which may include areas within the cargo bay 170 with differing widths, such as, for example, an area in which the width is reduced due to the wheel wells 579, or in a tapered section of an aft region 170a of the cargo bay 170). FIGS. 9A and 9B illustrate at least these features, which correspond to the claim recitations discussed above in at least some embodiments of the disclosure. Accordingly, it is submitted that the drawings show every feature of the invention as specified in the claims. Consequently, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of these objections.

The drawings are also objected to as requiring correction under 37 C.F.R. 1.121(d), with the Examiner asserting that FIGS. 5-14B need to be submitted in wire-frame model drawings. The attached Replacement Sheets, FIGS. 5-14B, have been amended to be wire-frame model drawings. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that this objection be withdrawn.
Claims 50-57 and 60-68 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement, in particular for the recitation in claim 50, "...wherein the

at least one cargo support segment comprises a fixed central region and opposing lateral end segments moveably coupled to the fixed region and moveable between a first position and a second position, the first position defining a first width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the constricted width and the second position defining a second width of the at least one cargo support segment that is less than the nominal width and greater than the constricted width..." and similar recitations in claim 60. The Examiner also alleges that the first and second width of the cargo support segment, as well as the constricted width, are not described or discussed in the specification. These claim recitations are properly supported in the specification and accompanying drawings.

As agreed upon with the Examiner during the interview, the as-filed specification includes sufficient description and illustrations of these recitations to reasonably convey possession by the inventors of the claimed invention to one skilled in the relevant art. For example, as discussed during the interview, as well as discussed above with regard to the drawing objections, the as-filed specification includes descriptions and illustrations of the varying widths of the interior cargo bay 170 of the aircraft 100, and the movement of the lateral ends 503 of the cargo bay floor segments 502 relative to the stationary region 505 of the cargo bay floor segments 502 that enables adjustment of the overall width of the cargo bay floor segments 502 to adapt to a corresponding width of the interior cargo bay. (Supra, pp. 8-9; see also, e.g., paragraphs [0068], [0079], [0107], and [0108], and FIGS. 5-9B of the published U.S. application.)

It is noted again that the as-filed specification states that, in at least some embodiments, the cargo bay 170 may include wheel wells 579 that protrude inwardly and reduce the width within which the cargo bay floor segments 502 may translate (i.e., the width between opposing wheel wells 579 is smaller than the width on opposing sides of the wheels wells 579 in a direction along the rails 174, as described at least in paragraphs [0107]-[0108] and shown at least in FIGS. 9A and 9B). The as-filed specification also states that, in at least some embodiments, the cargo bay 170 may taper, especially in the aft regions 170a, thus creating varying widths. (See paragraphs [0107]-[0108] of the published U.S. application.) The as-filed specification also notes that, in some embodiments, the removable cargo bay floor segments can be sized and shaped to span most or all of the available width of the lower cargo bay when in a desired position. (See paragraph [0068] of the published U.S. application.) Again, as agreed upon with the Examiner during the interview, this exemplary
disclosure, as well as the remainder of the as-filed specification, provides sufficient description to meet the written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.

Claims 58 and 59 were rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claim 53 of U.S. Pat. No. 11,560,230 to Poe (hereinafter "Poe"). It is noted that Poe does not include claim 53 (final claim in Poe is claim 42), and as such, it appears that this rejection was made in error. As such, withdrawal of the double patenting rejections is respectfully requested. Applicant notes that if the Examiner intended to cite to a different claim in Poe, and if a nonstatutory double patenting rejection is maintained, Applicant reserves the right to hold any such rejection in abeyance at least until the Examiner is otherwise willing to allow the application. Applicant request the Examiner contact the undersigned attorney if doing so will would be helpful in handling any nonstatutory double patenting rejection, or any other rejection for that matter.

Applicant submits that all claims are in condition for allowance, and allowance thereof is respectfully requested. The Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned attorney for Applicant if such communication is deemed to expedite prosecution of this application.

The USPTO is hereby authorized to charge any deficiency in the fees filed with this paper, asserted to be filed with this paper, or which should have been filed with this paper to our Deposit Account No. 100435, under Docket No. RADIA-0006-USCNT1 | 88042-375707.
